newsitem.title: UK: Gasoline-led rally boosts IPE before early close.
newsitem.headline: Gasoline-led rally boosts IPE before early close.

text.p: IPE oil futures trading closed early on Friday with a strong late rally on the back of strength in the U.S. gasoline market, brokers said.

IPE Brent last traded 10 cents higher at $18.54 a barrel. Earlier it held in a narrow range in negative terrority before New York business began and values shut upwards. IPE gas oil also jumped, to last move $2.25 higher at $167.50 a tonne.
A power failure forced the exchange to close early.
"U.S. gasoline broke through 62.50, found some buying, then took off from there and that spilled over into the rest of the complex," said one broker.

The premature close concentrated late business into just one hour of frantic activity, with people quickly unwinding short positions before the weekend and much buying triggered by technical indicators in the rising market.
"This was a stop-driven rally, $18.50 was big stop to break through on the (Brent) crude," said one broker, "the early finish was definetly an artificial boost."

The upward surge defied earlier predictions that uncertainty over the U.N.'s negotiations with Iraq over an aid distribution plan would prompt most players to enter the weekend with balanced positions.

Iraq, which insists the aid plan be agreed before it resumes exporting crude, has to present further documents to the U.N. this weekend. Final approval by Secretary-General Kofi Annan is expected from mid to late next week.

The market strength also saw NYMEX crude toy with the $20 a barrel level. At 1510 gmt September crude appeared to have broken through to trade at $20.05, but it was unclear if the momentum existed for the break to hold.
Dealers said there appeared to be no fundamentals driving prices upwards, although tight North Sea crude markets were generally supportive.
